name: What this system does with the rules

text.content:
Generated from the system's own rules audit. It records what each screen does with the printed rules and where it has diverged — it is not a checklist of the rulebook.

The survey is finished: no entry is open on any screen. What it found and what it left are two different lists, and both are worth stating.

The resolution core was faithful and well cited from the start: the DM ladder, the eight difficulties, the six Effect bands, Boon/Bane, timeframes, range bands, the p.75 attack modifiers, Bulky/Very Bulky, Scope/Auto, the whole Core p.83-84 recovery chain, encumbrance, the armour skill penalty, Stun and the Effect-6 floor all match the books.

The divergences clustered in four places: the NPC person preset, the damage pipeline after the roll, psionics, and the initiative formula. All four are worked: initiative is done, the NPC person preset drains END first and its stored chains are migrated, the damage pipeline is closed end to end — Auto's three fire modes included — and psionics now spends: the listed cost on a success, one point on a failure, the excess below zero as damage, and reach paid for at twice or four times the price. The pipeline now spends ammunition too: a weapon records what is loaded, an attack takes its rounds out of it, a magazine that cannot pay refuses the shot, and a spare magazine puts the whole capacity back for the Minor Action Core folio 75 charges.

Two habits account for most of what the audit found, and both should outlive it. Verify against the corpus, never against the skill — two entries were graded against the mgt2-rules skill's paraphrase and were wrong for it, and both were withdrawn with the printed quote rather than "fixed" in code that was already right. And measure the payload, not the code — the one real defect found late (§8 D's ion reaching the attack payload and not the apply payload) was invisible to reading and obvious to a measurement, because the damage pipeline names a target-side trait in two places.

Severity

Meaning
AProduces a wrong number at the table. Fix before anything else.
BA printed rule the system never applies, where the data to apply it is already present.
CA gap: the rule is absent and the screen offers no route to it.
DFriction, stale comment, or dead code. No wrong number, but it misleads.

What this screen gets right

  • Effect and melee STR DM added to the damage roll [Core p.78]
  • a burst adding the Auto score, beside those two and outside the Reduced/Minimum transform [Core folio 79]
  • Destructive multiplying the rolled total by 10, from the doubled D or the trait [Core p.79]
  • Protection subtracted, AP ignoring that much of it, Lo-Pen multiplying it [Core p.78, FC p.8]
  • a spacecraft-scale target ignoring AP from a Ground weapon [Core p.80]
  • an Effect 6+ attack always inflicting at least 1 point [Core p.78]
  • Stun taken off END alone, the excess reported as rounds of incapacitation [Core p.80]
  • Ground/Spacecraft ×10 and ÷10 with rounding down, applied after Effect and Destructive and before the armour deduction [Core p.168, folio 167]
  • the mount's own damage multiple applied after the armour deduction [HG p.30, Core p.169]
  • the five Companion damage-response traits, and the rule that an excepted damage type gets through in full [Companion p.94-95]
